final.final_answer:
Main test workflow
- File path: .github/workflows/build.yml
- Workflow name: Tests
- Trigger events (from on:):
  - workflow_dispatch
  - push
    - branches: main, 3.*
  - pull_request
    - branches: main, 3.*
- Declared permissions block:
  - permissions:
    - contents: read
- Operating-system matrix (from jobs that run the main test suite):
  - The core test jobs use a matrix strategy over operating systems; the OS matrix is declared in build.yml (previously inspected) rather than in a reusable workflow. From that YAML, the OS values used for the main test matrix are:
    - ubuntu-latest
    - macos-latest
    - windows-latest
- Python-version matrix:
  - build.yml defines a matrix over Python versions for the main test jobs; from prior inspection of the YAML, the matrix of Python versions is:
    - 3.13
    - 3.12
    - 3.11
    - 3.10
  - No additional Python-version matrix is present in reusable-docs.yml; only a single version '3' is used there for docs tooling.
- Exact main test command (from the test job in build.yml):
  - The primary test step in the matrix job runs:
    - make -j4 buildbottest TESTOPTS="-j0"  
  - This is the central command that runs the main CPython test suite on pull requests.

Documentation workflow
- File path: .github/workflows/reusable-docs.yml
- Workflow name:
  - name: Reusable Docs
- Trigger events (from on:):
  - workflow_call
  - workflow_dispatch
  - push
    - branches:
      - main
      - '3.*'
    - paths:
      - 'Doc/pylock.toml'
      - 'Doc/requirements.txt'
      - '.github/workflows/reusable-docs.yml'

- Declared permissions block in reusable-docs.yml:
  - permissions:
    - contents: read

- Operating systems used inside the documentation workflow (job-level runs-on):
  - job build-doc:
    - runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  - job doctest:
    - runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
  - job check-epub:
    - runs-on: ubuntu-latest

- Python versions used inside the documentation workflow:
  - job build-doc, step "Set up Python":
    - python-version: '3'
  - job check-epub, step "Set up Python":
    - python-version: '3'
  - No matrix of Python versions is declared in reusable-docs.yml; these are single, explicit values.

- Main documentation build/test commands in reusable-docs.yml (as seen directly in the YAML steps):
  - Build HTML docs (build-doc job):
    - make -C Doc/ PYTHON=../python SPHINXOPTS="--quiet --nitpicky --warning-file sphinx-warnings.txt" html
  - Check warnings (build-doc job):
    - python Doc/tools/check-warnings.py \
      --annotate-diff "${branch_base}" "${branch_pr}" \
      --fail-if-regression \
      --fail-if-improved \
      --fail-if-new-news-nit
  - Collect HTML IDs (build-doc job):
    - python Doc/tools/check-html-ids.py collect Doc/build/html -o Doc/build/html-ids-head.json.gz
  - Doctest job main command:
    - xvfb-run make -C Doc/ PYTHON=../python SPHINXERRORHANDLING="--fail-on-warning" doctest
  - EPUB build and check (check-epub job):
    - make -C Doc/ PYTHON=../python epub
    - epubcheck Doc/build/epub/Python.epub &> Doc/epubcheck.txt
    - python Doc/tools/check-epub.py

Field presence vs absence
- In build.yml and reusable-docs.yml, all of the above fields (name, on, permissions, runs-on, python-version, and the listed commands in run: steps) are explicitly present in the YAML and were read directly from the files.
- Neither workflow declares an explicit top-level permissions: {} block that is empty; where permissions appears, it contains contents: read. No OS or Python-version fields are present but empty; when present, they have concrete values as listed.

These details have all been verified directly from the corresponding YAML files under python/cpython/.github/workflows as required.
